sourceTitle: The Last Cup: A Film That Does Not Let Us Look Away
scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original film-review and environmental reading assessment, requiring independent linguistic and pedagogical validation

questions.q: What is the red plastic cup mainly used to represent in the opening?
choices: A new product the concert hall intends to sell.
Waste that remains after an event has ended.
A mistake made by the documentary's director.
An environmental law introduced by the town.
questions.explanation: The cup remains after the entertainment, symbolising waste that is usually no longer visible to visitors.

questions.q: How does the contrast between cheerful music and arriving cleaners affect the opening?
choices: It shows that the concert was poorly attended.
It suggests that cleaners dislike music.
It makes the scene look like a safety warning.
It draws attention to work that starts when the celebration finishes.
questions.explanation: The juxtaposition highlights the invisible labour following the enjoyable event.

questions.q: Why does the reviewer prefer the cleaner's explanation to an image of a trapped animal?
choices: The cleaner speaks more clearly than the teenagers.
The animal image would be too expensive to film.
The conversation reveals schedules, costs and people behind the problem.
The reviewer thinks wildlife has no connection with plastic pollution.
questions.explanation: The cleaner's account makes the litter problem concrete through logistics and responsibility.

questions.q: What was the teenagers' main obstacle when planning drinks for their event?
choices: The cheapest supplier used only disposable packaging.
The beach concert could not have any visitors.
The school canteen refused to lend equipment.
Guests could not bring their own containers.
questions.explanation: Their cheapest supplier provided only single-use bottles, prompting an alternative plan.

questions.q: What does Kent's treatment of the chaotic first evening suggest?
choices: She doubts young organisers can make useful decisions.
She refuses to show any mistakes made at the event.
She presents their imperfect efforts with some sympathy.
She blames the teenagers for failing to create an ideal system.
questions.explanation: The filmmaker shows the messy first attempt without ridiculing the teenagers.

questions.q: Which issue makes carrying a reusable cup less straightforward for some people?
choices: Venue security rules and limited opportunities to wash a cup.
Every reusable cup has to be made of glass.
All visitors are asked to pay the same high deposit.
Concerts usually provide free cleaning equipment.
questions.explanation: The review mentions a venue prohibiting containers and a visitor unable to wash a cup conveniently.

questions.q: What is the reviewer's main objection to the film's treatment of individual responsibility?
choices: It refuses to ask viewers to change their habits.
It mentions practical constraints but moves past them too quickly.
It recommends too many different environmental policies.
It focuses mainly on the physical properties of plastic.
questions.explanation: The difficulties briefly appear, then are displaced by a broad message about personal choice.

questions.q: Why do the reported costs of the deposit system matter?
choices: They prove that all cup deposits are a waste of public money.
They show that buying single-use cups was never cheaper.
They demonstrate that the teenagers designed a perfect scheme.
They allow viewers to assess benefits alongside practical limitations.
questions.explanation: The documentary is strongest when it publishes costs and acknowledges uncertain long-term savings.

questions.q: What would the reviewer prefer instead of the beautiful closing shot?
choices: A longer concert scene with more cheerful music.
A summary of the director's earlier films.
A practical discussion about who will keep the system working.
A warning that no school should organise beach concerts.
questions.explanation: A meeting about emptying bins would direct attention to ongoing responsibility.

questions.q: Which description captures the reviewer's final judgement?
choices: The film is useful if viewers question its simplifications.
Its flaws make it unsuitable for any school event.
Its only achievement is the quality of the images.
The reviewer believes the film presents no realistic solutions.
questions.explanation: The closing recommendation values the film's honesty while urging critical viewing.
